name: tier3_e10_cert
source: EPA National Vehicle and Fuel Emissions Laboratory (NVFEL) (a) Fuel Analysis Report 26781, '2018 Toyota 2.5L A25A-FKS Engine Tier 3 Fuel - Test Data Package', Version 2020-07 (Ann Arbor, MI: US EPA, National Center for Advanced Technology, 2020) and (b) the accompanying Test Data Package (the xlsx workbook) - PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7 review round 1 F3: these are two separate documents from the same NVFEL package and are cited separately below, not conflated. The EPA Tier 3 Bin 30 regular-grade certification fuel (10 vol% ethanol) this project's toyota_a25a_fks.json engine's fuel_map was measured on. MEASURED (Report 26781, method in parens): Net Heating Value (ASTM D240) = 18037.00 BTU/lb; Carbon Content (ASTM D5291) = 82.99 wt%; Hydrogen Content (ASTM D5291) = 13.43 wt%; Total Oxygen (ASTM D5599) = 3.58 wt% (C+H+O sums to exactly 100.00 wt%); Specific Gravity @ 60/60 deg F (ASTM D4052) = 0.74400; Density @ 60 deg F (ASTM D4052) = 0.74326 g/cm^3; Ethanol content (ASTM D5599) = 9.66 vol%. METHOD DISAGREEMENT (PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7 review F3): Report 26781 states its Net Heating Value method as ASTM D240 (the 18037.00 BTU/lb figure used below); SAE 2019-01-0249 (Kargul et al., 'Benchmarking a 2018 Toyota Camry 2.5-Liter Atkinson Cycle Engine with Cooled-EGR')'s own Table 4, 'EPA Tier 3 Certification Fuel' column, instead cites ASTM D3338 for a lower-precision 41.9 MJ/kg figure - the two sources disagree on which standard was actually used for the heating-value measurement. This file's lhv_j_kg is derived from Report 26781's own D240-cited 18037.00 BTU/lb value, not from SAE Table 4's rounded D3338 number; SAE Table 4's other figures (SG 0.74400, Carbon wt 0.8299) do match Report 26781's raw values exactly, so the cross-check below still stands for everything except the method label on the heating value. DERIVED lhv_j_kg: 18037.00 BTU/lb * (1055.05585262 J / 0.45359237 kg) [exact BTU(IT)-to-J and lb-to-kg conversion factors] = exactly 18037 * 2326 = 41954062 J/kg (the conversion factor 1055.05585262/0.45359237 reduces to exactly 2326, since both the BTU(IT)-to-J and lb-to-kg conversions are themselves exact by definition - no rounding, no '...4...' remainder) = 41954062.0 J/kg (41.954062 MJ/kg; matches the SAE Table 4 rounded figure of 41.9-41.95 MJ/kg). DERIVED density_kg_m3: 0.74326 g/cm^3 * 1000 = 743.26 kg/m^3 (matches SG 0.744 cross-check). DERIVED afr_stoich via Heywood 1988 section 3.2's air/fuel stoichiometry from the measured elemental mass fractions (brief-specified method): mass fractions C=0.8299, H=0.1343, O=0.0358 (sum 1.0000); molar amounts per gram fuel n_C = C/12.011 = 0.069095, n_H = H/1.008 = 0.133234, n_O = O/15.999 = 0.002238 mol/g (PHYS-033 P4 I7a C7 review F3: n_C was previously printed as 0.069103, a transcription/rounding error in this prose only - 0.8299/12.011 = 0.069095; the stored afr_stoich value below was always computed from full-precision floats, not from these rounded printed intermediates, so it is unaffected); oxygen required for complete combustion n_O2_req = n_C + n_H/4 - n_O/2 = 0.069095 + 0.033308 - 0.001119 = 0.1012847 mol O2/g fuel (previously printed as 0.101292, propagating the same n_C rounding error - also prose-only); one mole of atmospheric O2 is accompanied by 3.773 mol of 'atmospheric nitrogen' (N2 + trace gases lumped, molar mass 28.16 g/mol, Heywood 1988 section 3.2's air model), so air mass per mole O2 = M_O2 + 3.773*M_N2_atm = 31.998 + 3.773*28.16 = 138.24568 g/mol O2; afr_stoich = n_O2_req * 138.24568 = 14.002173341183884 (dimensionless kg air / kg fuel, computed from full float precision, correct and unchanged by the F3 prose fix). Cross-checks the brief's own rough estimate of ~13.96 to within 0.3%. Computation reproduced by out/c7/compute_fuel.py in the physics_sim worktree and independently re-derived (to full float precision) by tests/unit/test_cited_engine_data.cpp's own AFR recomputation.

knock.source: [C] EPA NVFEL Fuel Analysis Report 26781 (the same report as this file's LHV): Research Octane Number (ASTM D2699) 92.0, Motor Octane Number (ASTM D2700) 84.0, (R+M)/2 88.00, sensitivity 8.0 (Paragon Laboratories, 9/20/2017). The engine's own requirement: SAE 2019-01-0249 states 87 AKI regular fuel.
